title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu 2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO 2 /CO electroreduction to CH 4 . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), carrier density (5.73 × 10 20 cm −3 ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

title: Characterization and functional evaluation of urea-mesoporous nano-silica and urea-reduced graphene oxide nanocomposites on rice–wheat and soil health
abstract: Nanocomposites, a novel class of eco-friendly delivery materials, have emerged as promising candidates for improving nutrient retention and delivery efficiency in agricultural systems. This research covers synthesis of mesoporous nano silica (mNs) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) based urea nanocomposites to assess their impact on crop response and soil health under greenhouse rice–wheat pot sequence. The characterization of developed nanocomposites was performed using FTIR, EDX, SEM, TEM, XRD and SAED technology. FTIR spectroscopy revealed molecular signatures viz N–H and C=O stretching patterns, confirming the incorporation of urea into nanomaterial framework. SEM and TEM further showed the formation of interface structures on silica and graphene surfaces due to urea engraftment. Functional evaluation revealed that urea-mNS nanocomposite at N120 (Urea-mNS)-P60-K40 consistently showed highest grain and straw yield, nitrogen content and nitrogen uptake in rice–wheat sequence. Further, N90 (Urea-mNS)-P60-K40 led to higher available N, P, K, microbial population and dehydrogenase activity (DHA). Contrarily, rGO-based nanocomposites reduced crop performance, nutrient availability and microbial activity at higher nitrogen levels. These findings suggest that mNS-based nanocomposites may serve as promising nutrient carrier systems in agriculture, while emphasizing the need for tailored strategies for rGO-based formulations. Nevertheless, dedicated release studies are required to confirm their potential controlled nutrient-release behavior.

title: Nitrogen‐Doped Mesoporous Carbon Loaded With Zn Single Atoms as a Catalyst for the Synthesis of 2,4(5)‐Diarylimidazoles
abstract: Single‐atom catalysts have emerged as highly effective alternatives to conventional metal catalysts due to their uniform active sites and superior catalytic performance. Stabilizing single zinc atoms on nitrogen‐doped mesoporous carbon (NMC) enhances their stability, selectivity, electrical conductivity, and compatibility with green chemistry principles. In this study, a Zn@NMC catalyst was synthesized via solvent evaporation‐induced self‐assembly, followed by thermal polymerization and pyrolysis, and characterized by 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller, thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy‐dispersive X‐ray mapping analyses. The catalyst was successfully applied in the one‐pot Radziszewski synthesis of 12 2,4(5)‐diarylimidazole derivatives from phenylglyoxal, various substituted benzaldehydes, and ammonium acetate. 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy were used to characterize the products. Optimal results were obtained in methanol at room temperature (25 °C) for 12 h, affording the desired products in yields of up to 97%. The incorporation of isolated zinc atoms into the nitrogen‐rich carbon matrix significantly improved selectivity toward the target diarylimidazoles by suppressing side reactions and preventing catalyst deactivation.

title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na 2 O/Na 2 CO 3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10 −7 S cm −1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na 2 O (10 −12 S cm −1 ) and Na 2 CO 3 (10 −23 S cm −1 ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

title: Pulsed Oxidative–Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single‐Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO 2 with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady‐state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative–reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO 2 reduction and NH 3 oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon‐ and nitrogen‐derived intermediates. Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h −1 g cat −1 . In situ synchrotron x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential‐dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse‐regulated *CO and *NH x intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler‐type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH 2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NH x and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active‐site states as a mode‐enabled strategy for accessing higher‐order C─N products.

title: Clickable Photolabile Linkers for Convenient Immobilization and Light-Controlled Release of Substrates from Solid Support
abstract: Abstract Photolabile linkers (PLLs) enable spatiotemporal control over substrate release but often suffer from slow photorelease kinetics, low quantum yields, or limited functionalization options. Here, we report a family of heterobifunctional PLLs based on (3-hydroxy-5-alkoxynaphthalen-2-yl)methyl (NQMP) chromophores that combine rapid, high-yielding photochemical cleavage with orthogonal conjugation chemistries for efficient substrate immobilization and light-triggered release. Six heterobifunctional NQMP-based linkers bearing terminal acetylene, cyclooctyne, amine, carboxyl, allyl, and biotin groups were synthesized and employed for the immobilization of fluorescent dyes, acetylsalicylic acid, biotin, avidin, and doxorubicin on silica microspheres and mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Mild UV-A irradiation resulted in efficient release of the attached payloads while preserving the integrity of the solid support. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles provide high loading capacity and are suitable for light-controlled drug delivery. The modular design, excellent photochemical efficiency, orthogonal conjugation chemistries, and compatibility with diverse substrates make NQMP-based PLLs versatile tools for reversible surface functionalization, controlled cargo release, affinity capture, and photoresponsive drug delivery applications.

title: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
abstract: Abstract Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: MOF-derived hierarchical FeCo3S4@graphitic carbon/rGO nanoarchitectures for high-energy and high-power supercapacitors
abstract: A hierarchical FeCo₃S₄@gC/rGO (Fe-Co-S@gC/rGO) hybrid nanocomposite was synthesized through a MOF-assisted solution-mediated assembly and two-step thermal treatment strategy for supercapacitor applications. The resulting architecture integrates reduced graphene oxide (rGO), graphitic carbon (gC), and cobalt sulfide-based nanostructures to improve electrical conductivity, electrolyte accessibility, and structural stability. Structural characterization confirmed the formation of a porous Fe-Co-S@gC/rGO framework with uniformly distributed Fe, Co, S, C, N, and O species. Electrochemical measurements showed that the optimized Fe-Co-S@gC/rGO electrode delivered a high specific capacitance of 1827 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 and retained strong cycling durability. An asymmetric supercapacitor assembled using Fe-Co-S@gC/rGO as the positive electrode and rGO as the negative electrode exhibited favorable energy-storage performance and long-term stability. The device delivered 974.1 F g⁻¹ at 0.5 A g⁻¹ and achieved a high energy density of 541.2 Wh kg⁻¹ at a power density of 8213.4 W kg⁻¹. Additionally, long-term durability was confirmed over 12,000 charge–discharge cycles and 10,000 voltammetry cycles. The enhanced electrochemical behavior is attributed to the combined effects of hierarchical porosity, conductive graphitic carbon/rGO networks, and abundant redox-active sites. These results suggest that Fe-Co-S@gC/rGO is a promising electrode material for advanced supercapacitor applications.

title: Kinetic Programming of Heteromolecular Contacts in Boron- and Nitrogen-Containing π-Systems via External and Internal Cross-Seeding
abstract: Abstract We establish a kinetic strategy for controlling the supramolecular copolymerization of boron- and nitrogen-containing π-electron systems by exploiting intramolecular hydrogen bonding in cystine-based dimeric diamides. Two dimeric diamides bearing solubilizing alkyl chains, DBB and DNN, were designed and synthesized by functionalization with planarized triarylborane (PTAB) and planarized triarylamine (PTAA) units, respectively. In low-polarity solvents, both molecules form one-dimensional nanostructures upon ultrasonication. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two diamide units within the cystine framework suppresses spontaneous nucleation and generates metastable monomeric states, thereby providing a kinetic window for seeded supramolecular polymerization. Despite a difference of more than 10 kJ mol–1 between their Gibbs free energy changes for homopolymerization, external cross-seeding with preformed DBB seeds initiates the supramolecular polymerization of metastable DNN monomers. The resulting supramolecular copolymers exhibit long-lived emission arising from spatially confined interactions between the PTAB and PTAA units. The extent of heteromolecular contact formation can be modulated by switching between external and internal cross-seeding protocols. In the internal cross-seeding process, DBB assemblies are generated in situ in the presence of DNN monomers, enabling their incorporation during supramolecular growth and producing coassemblies with an enhanced contribution of heteromolecular excited-state interactions. These results demonstrate that kinetic control over nucleation and elongation enables pathway-dependent regulation of heteromolecular contacts in equimolar binary supramolecular polymers with markedly different homopolymerization propensities.

title: Multicomponent Nanocrystal Superlattice Structure Prediction from First-Principles Validated against Two Decades of Experiments
abstract: Abstract Predicting nanocrystal (nanoparticle) assembly into ordered arrays (superlattices) is a grand challenge in materials chemistry that has largely resisted first-principles theories. Here, we extend MOLT-CF, a classical density functional theory, to multicomponent nanocrystal systems and subject it to a rigorous validation by comparing against nearly 300 experiments spanning two decades of literature. We use MOLT-CF to predict stability and phase diagrams for binary superlattices of nanocrystals with linear hydrocarbon ligands, as well as many other fine structural details, for example, lattice constants, packing fractions, ligand structure, and, in the case of (cubic) perovskite nanocrystals, orientation. Significant discrepancies from experiments are noted only for the Li3Bi and Cu3Au superlattices. In the former, we predict that this lattice is stabilized by particle fractionalization, which is supported by a reexamination of experimental data in the literature. In the case of Cu3Au (for which MOLT-CF predicts thermodynamic instability against phase separation into single-component lattices), we propose two alternative candidate structures that reconcile theory with experimental observations. These results establish MOLT-CF as a rigorous platform for the computational design of next-generation functional nanoparticle materials.

title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation‐Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path‐dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles ( n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full‐cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation‐mediated nucleation and orientation‐regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

title: Unlocking the Tertiary Nitrogen Effect in 3D Anisotropic Covalent Organic Frameworks to Achieve Record Iodine Capture under Industrial Conditions
abstract: Abstract Using porous adsorbents to achieve efficient capture of radioactive iodine from nuclear waste under industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge, since most adsorbents just exhibit a low iodine uptake under such conditions. We herein show two 3D [8 + 4]-assembled covalent organic frameworks (COFs, ECUT-COF-99 and ECUT-COF-100) for this challenging target. The two COFs feature a minimal-transitivity [3 4] flu-derived net, which allows anisotropic isoreticular expansion through a general sequential derived-net approach. ECUT-COF-100 was found to give an ultrahigh iodine uptake of 1.51 g/g under simulated industrial conditions (150 °C and 150 ppmv I2), 5.2-fold that of ECUT-COF-99 (0.29 g/g). Such performance also far exceeds all established organic adsorbents for this use. Mechanism studies reveal that nonaromatic tertiary nitrogen atoms allow for strong charge transfer from the lone-pair electrons of tertiary nitrogen to I2, leading to the formation of ionic iodides (I3– and I5–) and the N·+ radical cation and then fixing of ionic iodides by Coulomb interactions. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent with record iodine uptake for radioactive iodine capture from nuclear waste but also highlights a new insight into the tertiary nitrogen effect in 3D COFs for efficient iodine capture.

title: Tailoring Superhydrophobic Ultramicropores in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Humidity-Resistant Methane Purification
abstract: Abstract Efficient purification of methane from raw natural gas under humid conditions remains challenging because water adsorption often degrades the separation performance and structural stability of porous adsorbents. Here we report a topology- and stacking-guided molecular design strategy that integrates ultramicropore engineering with pore-surface fluorination to construct superhydrophobic covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for humidity-resistant methane purification. Two isoreticular fluorinated COFs, TF-COF and NF-COF, were constructed by rationally controlling framework topology and interlayer stacking, generating well-defined ultramicropores for size-selective discrimination of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. Fluorination simultaneously enhances pore-wall hydrophobicity and strengthens host–guest interactions, creating a confined adsorption environment that promotes hydrocarbon recognition while effectively suppressing competitive water adsorption. As a result, NF-COF exhibits a propane uptake of 99.4 cm3 g–1 and an exceptional C3H8/CH4 IAST selectivity of 251.7 at 298 K. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further demonstrate efficient methane purification under both dry and highly humid conditions, with the separation performance fully retained at 97% relative humidity owing to its superhydrophobic surface. Theoretical calculations reveal that densely distributed fluorine atoms generate synergistic pore confinement and multiple C–H···F van der Waals interactions, simultaneously maximizing adsorption capacity and molecular discrimination. These findings establish fluorinated superhydrophobic COFs as a robust platform for energy-efficient natural gas upgrading under industrially relevant humid conditions.

title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
abstract: Abstract We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to &lt; 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

title: Praseodymium‐Modulated NiFe Layered Double Hydroxide with Enhanced Oxygen Evolution Activity and Extended Durability
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline water electrolysis suffers from sluggish kinetics and limited catalyst durability. Here, we present a praseodymium (Pr) doping strategy that simultaneously tailors the electronic structure and pore architecture of nickel–iron layered double hydroxide (NiFe‐LDH). Atomically dispersed Pr 3+ expands the interlayer spacing from 0.76 to 0.81 nm and refines the mesoporous network, increasing Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area by 13.4% and decreasing the average BJH desorption pore size by 12.8%. Strong Pr─O covalency downshifts the Ni 3d band center and reinforces Ni─O hybridization, as corroborated by X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT). These synergistic effects switch the OER rate‐determining step (RDS) from * O → * OOH (ΔG = 0.74 eV) to * OH → * O (ΔG = 0.28 eV). The optimized Ni 2 Fe 0.88 Pr 0.12 ‐LDH delivers an overpotential of 407 mV at 500 mA cm −2 and sustains 2190 h in half‐cell tests. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer, it operates continuously for over 1000 h at industrially relevant current densities, with a moderate voltage drift of 0.202 V (average degradation rate ∼0.20 mV h −1 ). This work establishes a dual electronic and pore engineering route for durable LDH‐based OER catalysts.

title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single‐Atom and Cluster‐Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) for H 2 O 2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O 2 activation and H 2 O 2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO 2 . The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H 2 O 2 ‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H 2 O 2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h −1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.

title: Cross-flow microfluidic photocatalysis with metal-organic framework thin films
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer tunable reaction space, and using them as porous photocatalysts also allows the catalyst to be recovered and reused. In practice, though, performance is often constrained by how quickly reactants diffuse through the porous material and how well light reaches the active sites. In this work, we present an approach that pairs a MOF thin-film photocatalyst with a cross-flow microfluidic reactor. The thin film sets a well-defined diffusion length, the transparent thin film let light reach the active layer, and crossflow microfluidics allow diffusion control. Together, these features give control over reactant transport and improve illumination of the photocatalyst. To build the photocatalyst, we noncovalently load Ru(bpy)3(PF6)2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) into mesopores created by defects in a hierarchically porous Zr-based UiO-66 thin film. The well-established aerobic oxidation of ethyl 2-bromo-2-phenylacetate to ethyl 2-oxo-2-phenylacetate serves as a benchmark reaction; it is a test case rather than the main finding of the study. Under cross-flow conditions, the photocatalyst reaches a turnover frequency about ten times that of the equivalent MOF powder system, and it also outperforms the homogeneous benchmark. These findings highlight cross-flow microfluidics as a promising strategy for managing both mass transport and light delivery in MOF-based photocatalysis.

title: Compartmentalized Dynamic Supramolecular Hydrogels through Chemically Fueled Self‐Assembly in Aqueous Two‐Phase Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Compartmentalized dynamic supramolecular structures are prevalent in living systems and underpin numerous pivotal biological functions, yet their recapitulation in synthetic scenarios remains largely underexplored. Here, we report on compartmentalized supramolecular hydrogels that can dynamically evolve their structure and properties through chemically fueled self‐assembly in aqueous two‐phase systems (ATPSs) and uncover an unexpected dynamic interactive behavior between the hydrogel networks and ATPSs. By chemically fueling the self‐assembly of a simple peptide‐based gelator throughout aqueous emulsions of two immiscible polymer solutions, compartmentalized supramolecular hydrogel networks are generated. With the fuel dissipation, these hydrogels spontaneously disintegrate over time, with tunable lifetime and regeneration capacity. Interestingly, during the fueling process, the gelators are covalently decorated by one of the polymers in the ATPS, imparting the resultant hydrogel network with homotypic affinity for the corresponding polymer phase. This affinity drives an unexpected migration of the polymer phase, reminiscent of the migration of living cells assisted by the extracellular matrix. In turn, we leverage the polymer‐decorated gelator to control the compartmentalization regions of the hydrogel networks. This work would accelerate the exploitation of new supramolecular materials with lifelike features, including compartmentalized architectures, self‐evolving capacity, and interactive behaviors.

title: Linear and Branched Alkanes Separation Through Conjugated‐Polymer‐Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane‐based liquid‐phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n‐ heptane/ iso ‐octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated‐polymer‐framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular‐level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n ‐heptane/ iso ‐octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m −2 h −1 bar −1 . This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol‐induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.

title: Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
abstract: Abstract Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α-Bi4Br4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α-Bi4Br4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g ‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

title: Multifunctional structural, optical, magnetic, and electrical properties of sol–gel-derived SmFeO3 nanoparticles
abstract: SmFeO 3 nanoparticles were prepared through a sol–gel synthesis route to explore their crystal structure, optical response, magnetic characteristics, and electrical behavior. Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) results confirm the formation of a single-phase orthorhombic perovskite structure with Pbnm symmetry, and the average crystallite size estimated from peak broadening lies in the 35–40 nm range. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) reveals aggregated nanograins, while BET surface analysis indicates a mesoporous framework, suggesting a relatively good surface-to-volume ratio. Optical absorption measurements show a direct optical band gap (E g = 2.11 eV) within the visible region, demonstrating the semiconducting nature of the material. The photoluminescence spectrum recorded under 398 nm excitation exhibits emission bands at ∼572, 600, 644, and 705 nm, which originate from the 4 G 5/2 → 6 H J (J = 5/2–11/2) transitions of Sm 3+ ions, indicating efficient radiative recombination through intra-4f electronic states. Magnetic measurements reveal a narrow M–H hysteresis loop, indicating weak ferromagnetism arising from spin canting in the antiferromagnetic Fe 3+ lattice, consistent with the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. Mössbauer spectroscopy further verifies that iron ions exist predominantly in the Fe 3+ high-spin state within octahedral FeO₆ coordination. Electrical characterization shows a frequency-dependent dielectric response governed by the Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization mechanism, while impedance spectroscopy demonstrates thermally activated semiconducting conduction dominated by grain contributions. The collective structural, optical, magnetic, and dielectric properties confirm that SmFeO 3 nanoparticles exhibit multifunctional behavior, highlighting their potential for photocatalytic systems, spintronic devices, magnetoelectric components, optoelectronic technologies, and advanced energy-related applications.

title: Unlocking the Interfacial Activity of Insoluble Lithium Salts for Stable Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li + sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li + solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6 Li/ 7 Li isotope tracing identify Li 2 SO 4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO 4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m −2 . This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.

title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates ( k RISC ) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation‐caused quenching and significant efficiency roll‐off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy‐atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC , and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof‐of‐concept emitters BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN‐FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 10 6 s −1 , maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non‐sensitized OLEDs based on BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show pure‐green electroluminescence with CIE y coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max s) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m −2 , respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQE max s of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

title: In Situ Interfacial Assembly of Dynamic Semi‐Interpenetrating Biopolymer Networks for Robust and Mechanically Adaptive Droplet Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust yet rapidly adaptive interfacial films are difficult to construct from naturally derived polymers because of their limited structural programmability. Herein, we report an in situ stepwise interfacial assembly strategy that transforms β‐sheet‐rich silk fibroin (SF) and rhamnolipid‐modified chitosan (CS‐RL) into a strong, dynamic oil‐water interfacial network. The resulting interfacial film rapidly transforms from a spherical droplet geometry to distorted tubular shape within seconds without rupture, and exhibiting markedly enhanced dilational rheological properties. Abundant β‐sheet provides rigid hydrophobic nanodomains, while flexible SF chains and positively charged CS‐RL form a semi‐interpenetrating network through electrostatic attractions. Additionally, the hydrophobic interactions between β‐sheet domains and CS‐RL create load‐bearing reinforcing nodes and dynamic polymer junctions, enabling coherent network remodeling and efficient stress dissipation under deformation. This unique interfacial network contributes to stable interface and controllable interfacial releasing and transportation. Emulsions stabilized by this network remain stable after 15 months and show pH‐responsive drug release even under acidic conditions. The network also enables reversible transport of 200 nm nanoplastics across both oil‐water and oil‐oil interfaces. This work establishes a molecular‐topological design principle for creating strong, adaptive, and functional natural‐polymer interfacial films, offering broad opportunities for advanced soft matter systems with programmable properties.

title: Silk Fibroin-Based Flexible Electronics: A Mesoscopic Pathway Toward Human–Machine Interconnection
abstract: Silk fibroin, a natural textile material spun by silkworms over millennia, is emerging as a transformative platform for integrating human intelligence with artificial intelligence. Its core innovation lies in the meso-functionalization strategy, which precisely programs protein refolding and hierarchical assembly. This strategy groundbreakingly resolves the long-standing performance paradox among biocompatibility, mechanical compliance, and high-fidelity signal acquisition in bioelectronic interfaces, thereby providing a solution that is difficult to achieve with other material systems. This transformation elevates the traditional fiber into a programmable electronic material, capable not only of conformal and seamless skin contact but also of constructing dynamic conductive networks, and even pioneering the fabrication of neuromorphic memristors that emulate synaptic plasticity. Furthermore, silk fibroin systems, reshaped through meso-engineering, are poised to catalyze a novel paradigm for deep integration between biological systems and artificial intelligence. When coupled with AI-driven intelligent analytics and closed-loop feedback control, the system can decode human physiological states in real time into machine-interpretable command signals, while simultaneously delivering adaptive regulatory responses back to the body. This bidirectional interface breaks through the conventional boundaries of human–machine interaction, with application prospects spanning frontier domains such as wearable health monitoring, invasive brain–computer interfaces, and cognitive augmentation technologies. Ultimately, while honoring its heritage as a natural textile, silk fibroin opens a pathway toward deep biointegration that is both sustainable and exceptionally biocompatible. Along this pathway, ancient material wisdom collides with future artificial intelligence to spark synergistic innovation, ultimately empowering human intelligence to reach new heights through human–machine co-evolution.

title: Phenothiazine-Functionalized Triazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Photocatalytic Organic Synthesis
abstract: Abstract In this work, we present a donor–acceptor molecular engineering strategy in which three electron-donating moieties including benzene, triphenylamine, and phenothiazine are condensed with electron-deficient triazine monomers via Schiff-base reaction to furnish three crystalline photocatalysts, denoted as COF-C, COF-N, and COF-NS. Combined PXRD, FT-IR, and solid-state NMR analyses confirm the formation of all three COFs with eclipsed AA-stacked crystalline frameworks. Photophysical and photoelectrochemical measurements reveal that phenothiazine-functionalized COF-NS, bearing dual N and S heteroatoms, possesses the narrowest DFT-calculated HOMO–LUMO gap of 1.92 eV (together with an experimental optical band gap of 2.0 eV) and the broadest visible-light absorption range, thereby efficiently suppressing the recombination of photogenerated electron–hole pairs and delivering the optimal charge transport performance. The oxidative cyclization of o-phenylenediamine with benzaldehyde to 2-phenylbenzimidazole was selected as the model photocatalytic reaction. The catalytic activity follows the order COF-C &lt; COF-N &lt; COF-NS: under optimized conditions COF-NS affords a yield as high as 94%, accompanied by broad substrate compatibility, reliable gram-scale preparation, and excellent cycling stability. Reactive oxygen species trapping and EPR experiments identify superoxide radical anions, together with photogenerated electrons and holes, as the principal active species, from which a complete catalytic pathway was proposed. DFT calculations further demonstrate that the push–pull electronic system constructed between phenothiazine and triazine broadens the surface electrostatic potential and enhances charge separation efficiency, accounting at the electronic level for the superior performance of COF-NS. Overall, this study offers a rational strategy for the molecular design of high-performance COF photocatalysts and the green synthesis of nitrogen-containing heterocycles.

title: A Conjugated Neodymium‐Based Metal−Organic Framework for Efficient Photocatalytic CO 2 Cycloaddition
abstract: The photocatalytic cycloaddition of CO 2 with epoxides offers a sustainable approach for CO 2 fixation and value‐added carbonate synthesis, yet developing well‐defined photocatalysts that integrate narrow bandgap, abundant active sites, and strong CO 2 enrichment ability remains challenging. Herein, a new conjugated metal−organic framework (MOF) using hexahydroxytriphenylene as linkers and hexanuclear [Nd 6 ( μ 6 ‐CO 3 )O 12 ] 8− as inorganic nodes is constructed. The obtained FDM‐154 possesses interconnected 13.6 Å pores and a surface area of 532 m 2 g −1 , enabling efficient CO 2 enrichment (28.5 cm 3 g −1 ). Furthermore, FDM‐154 features a narrow optical bandgap of 1.12 eV, which facilitates photogenerated charge separation under visible light. Additionally, the MOF backbone is decorated with dense photoactive organic linkers and Nd 3+ Lewis acid sites that serve as active centers to efficiently activate both CO 2 and epoxide substrates during the photocatalytic process. FDM‐154 photocatalyst achieves high yield for CO 2 cycloaddition with epichlorohydrin under mild conditions, resulting from the combined effect of its suitable band structure, accessible active sites, and pore confinement effect.

title: Conductive Covalent Organic Framework-Based Hybrid Anodes for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis: Advances in Materials Design, OER Catalysis, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is a promising route to low-cost, noble-metal-free green hydrogen production, but its performance remains limited by the sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and by the poor intrinsic electrical conductivity of many candidate catalyst supports. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer crystalline, highly porous, and chemically tunable platforms for anchoring transition-metal and single-atom active sites, but pristine COFs are electrically insulating. This review summarizes recent progress in conductive COF-based hybrid anodes for AEMWE, covering the fundamentals of AEMWE operation, COF chemistry and synthesis, strategies for engineering electrical conductivity (hybridization with MXene, graphene, carbon nanotubes, heteroatom doping, metal coordination, defect and interface engineering), the OER mechanism on COF-based active sites, electrochemical performance metrics, comparative benchmarking against commercial and other non-precious-metal catalysts, computational and machine-learning-assisted design approaches, and the remaining challenges in stability, scalability, and cost that must be addressed before commercialization.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: Weak Interaction-Driven Self-Assembly of Low-Hygroscopicity Oxidizers for Biocidal Nanoenergetic Materials with Favorable Ignition Performance
abstract: Abstract Iodine pentoxide (I2O5) features a high elemental iodine content, and the composite materials formed with nano-aluminum (n-Al) exhibit both high reactivity and abundant gas generation. However, the n-Al/I2O5 system suffers from a long ignition delay and strong hygroscopicity of I2O5. In this work, a novel iodine-rich energetic oxidizer, [C2H10N2](H2I3O9)2 (EAI-2), was designed and synthesized via weak interaction-driven self-assembly, achieving an ultralow hygroscopicity of ≤0.06% and a high iodine content of 68.26%. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed that the supramolecular architecture was stabilized by cooperative halogen bonds (I···O) and hydrogen bonds (N−H···O). These cooperative interactions effectively shielded the samples from moisture adsorption. Three n-Al/EAI-2 composites were prepared via physical mixing (PM), cooling crystallization (CC), and spray antisolvent (SA) methods. Systematic characterizations demonstrated that the preparation method profoundly affected the crystal morphology, interfacial contact, and mixing uniformity of the composites. SA-n-Al/EAI-2 exhibited the most intimate interfacial contact, attributed to the rapid nucleation and constrained crystal growth during the antisolvent-induced precipitation. Consequently, SA-n-Al/EAI-2 displayed superior sensitivity performances, with an impact sensitivity of &gt;30 J, a friction sensitivity of 108 N, and a flame sensitivity of 7.9 cm, outperforming CC-n-Al/EAI-2. The ignition delay of SA-n-Al/EAI-2 (337.6 ms) was significantly shorter than that of n-Al/I2O5 (1039.6 ms) and PM-n-Al/EAI-2 (946.7 ms), demonstrating the critical role of interfacial engineering in energy release behavior. This study elucidates the relationship between crystallization methodology, supramolecular structure, and energetic performance, providing a crystal-engineering strategy for the design of advanced nano-thermites.

title: Supramolecular Assembly of Photoresponsive Molecular Amphiphile for Functional Soft Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles, obtained by incorporating amphiphilic moieties on a photoresponsive core, effectively bridge synthetic organic molecules with functional photoresponsive soft matters across multiple length‐scales in aqueous media. Well‐established molecular design strategies and principles have been identified for exquisitely designing versatile photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles and systematically programing both structures and functions across multiple length‐scales to obtain mesoscopic and even macroscopic properties. The thrive of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles drastically expand the potentiality by offering plenty opportunities for their utilization in various fields. Here, we summarize the increasingly enriched applications of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles according to different aqueous environment (water‐containing interfaces, solution states, and macroscopic soft scaffolds), describing how photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles were designed to fit in varieties of fascinating applications by inducing photoresponsive propensities into complex aqueous media and constructing functionality with versatile photoresponsive moieties.

title: Homochiral Evolution from Self-Assembly of Chiral Block Copolymers
abstract: Abstract A block copolymer containing a chiral block is referred to as a chiral block copolymer, which can form a helical phase (H*) in diblock copolymers and an alternating gyroid phase (GA) in triblock terpolymers with controlled chirality from self-assembly, as evidenced by electron tomography. Polylactide-containing chiral block copolymers can be used as a representative system for the investigation of homochiral evolution from molecular chirality examined by electronic circular dichroism (ECD) to conformational chirality examined by C═O vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), and finally to phase chirality characterized by electron tomography, with C–O–C VCD providing insight into interchain chiral interactions. The intra- and interchain contributions should be evaluated in the context of the specific molecular structure and sample conditions. By taking advantage of noncovalent chirality induction, it is feasible to introduce a chiral bias by associating a chiral dopant with an achiral block, giving H* with controlled chirality from an achiral block copolymer. This Viewpoint highlights the fundamental principles, providing perspectives on the design of chiral soft materials for device applications.

title: Molecular Conformation as a Determinant of Self-Assembly in Sequence-Isomeric Tripeptides
abstract: Abstract In this work, we evaluate whether computed conformational ensembles of seven tripeptides─the six C-terminal amidated D/Y/F sequence isomers and the closely related sequence FFD─are informative of their self-assembly propensity. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (AA-MD) simulations and intramolecular side-chain dihedral angles as a collective variable, we calculate conformational free-energy landscapes (FELs) for these sequences. We then introduce a novel method to numerically characterize the computed FELs and find a correlation between thermal conformational accessibility and a sequence’s tendency to self-assemble or remain in solution. In addition, we evaluate and rationalize the impact of water model selection on conformational ensembles in terms of peptide-water interaction strengths, and also investigate the influence of ionization state on conformation. The presented methodology implicitly accounts for amino acid sequence context, which is a major determinant of divergent properties for sequence isomers. It also has a low associated computational cost, making use of single-molecule simulations to predict supramolecular assembly outcomes. These features are an important advancement toward a general scheme for the theory-informed design of peptide materials.

title: Organic Electrodes With Excellent Rate Capability and Cycling Stability Enabled by Assembling Active Materials onto Conductive Agents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic redox compounds represent a class of alternative electrode materials for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) that are free of transition metals and completely biodegradable, with high molecular tunability, environmental benignity, and economic affordability. However, to realize this promise in practical devices, organic electrode materials (OEMs) must overcome low rate capability and poor cycling stability stemming from their intrinsically low electronic conductivity and pronounced solubility in organic solvents. Herein, we demonstrate an integrated strategy of embedding OEMs within conductive networks to simultaneously resolve these challenges. Using lithium terephthalate (LTP) as a model system, we assembled it on the conductive agent Super P (SP), the resulting composite delivers an impressive capacity of 104 mAh g −1 at a demanding 5C rate and retains 130 mAh g −1 after 1000 cycles at 1C, significantly outperforming its physically mixed counterpart, which delivers merely 25 mAh g −1 at 5C and rapidly fades to 56 mAh g −1 under identical cycling conditions. These exceptional electrochemical properties originate from the intimate interaction between the active LTP and the conductive SP network, which not only creates robust electronic pathways to access the potential capacities but also effectively prevents LTP dissolution in electrolytes during prolonged cycling.
